title: Pulling a constant out of a completed square
problem: An AI tutor found the minimum value of \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 12x + 23\) for real \(x\). Tap a slip if you spot one, or call it clean.
steps: Complete the square inside the parentheses by adding and subtracting \(9\): \(f(x) = 2(x^2 - 6x + 9 - 9) + 23\).
Pull the \(-9\) outside the parentheses, multiplying it by \(2\): \(f(x) = 2(x - 3)^2 - 18 + 23\).
Since \(2(x - 3)^2 \ge 0\) with equality at \(x = 3\), the minimum value is \(5\).

clean_steps: Complete the square inside the parentheses by adding and subtracting \(9\): \(f(x) = 2(x^2 - 6x + 9 - 9) + 23\).
Pull the \(-9\) outside the parentheses, multiplying it by \(2\): \(f(x) = 2(x - 3)^2 - 18 + 23\).
Since \(2(x - 3)^2 \ge 0\) with equality at \(x = 3\), the minimum value is \(5\).

meta.topic: Completing the square with a leading coefficient
meta.blurb: Factoring out \(2\) and pulling \(-9\) out as \(-18\) — easy spot to slip, did it?

explanation: Factoring \(2\) only from the \(x\)-terms and multiplying the pulled-out \(-9\) by \(2\) to get \(-18\) is exact: \(2(x-3)^2 + 5 = 2x^2 - 12x + 23\).
